items.title: Bildirim, aciliyet ve ilerleme göstergeleri
items.evidence_note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-31 on feat/rush-orchestrator at d4719cb (base 4f996e4). Dock-icon status indicators sourced ONLY from the shell's own freedesktop notification server (Quickshell.Services.Notifications; API surface and runtime semantics verified against the installed Quickshell 0.3.2 with throwaway D-Bus probes: Notification exposes hints (QVariantMap), desktopEntry, transient, expireTimeout, urgency and a closed(reason) signal with freedesktop NotificationClosed codes 1=Expired/2=Dismissed/3=CloseRequested; signals are imperatively connectable from QML JS; replaces_id updates the SAME tracked object in place via hintsChanged without a new notification signal; the server never auto-closes anything itself). (1) Count badge: a notification is ACTIVE from arrival until its native closed() signal fires. Close paths: user toast dismissal/action (dismiss), client-supplied positive expireTimeout (expire, honored by a 1s sweeper), client CloseNotification withdrawal, or activation of the app's dock icon (attention given; documented UX rule). expireTimeout -1 (never) and 0 (server default) persist until attended; transient notifications are expired once their toast hides (freedesktop: do not persist after display). Counts are exact server state, never estimated. (2) Urgency: critical (freedesktop urgency level 2) active notifications pulse an error-colored dot on the icon and tint the count badge red. (3) Progress: the freedesktop 'value' hint of active progress notifications, drawn as an arc (Canvas) around the icon; exact client-reported values normalized from 0..1 doubles or 0..100 percent, live-updated through replaces_id/hintsChanged; non-numeric values show no progress (never approximated). (4) Matching through ApplicationService.getAppById (desktop-entry hint, then icon name, then cleaned app name; generic dialog icons and absolute icon paths never identify an app); unmatched notifications badge nothing. Pure logic in the node-testable services/notifications/NotificationBadges.js pragma library. (5) Apps stacks aggregate member badges (summed count, OR'ed critical; progress deliberately NOT aggregated - one merged ring value would be arbitrary) and the aggregate outranks the DOCK-011 member-count badge; folder stacks show none. (6) Honest degradation: when ConfigService.notificationsEnabled is false the shell runs no notification server, so NO notification badges are shown (Plasma's own daemon owns the data; the active set is cleared on toggle-off). This is the documented default state (notificationsEnabled defaults to false). SCOPED OUT (blocked-on-bridge): KWin window-attention (demandsAttention) indicators. The resident KWin event bridge (services/kwin/scripts/kwin-event-bridge.js) does not forward demandsAttention (no windowRecord field, no signal connection), the compiled bridge plugin is not built in this checkout (2 pre-existing test skips) and the bridge is currently Intellihide-gated (WindowService bridgeLoader active only with anyDockIntellihide), so window attention is not honestly reachable without new low-level bridge protocol work and a KWin rig to verify it; asserted by test_dock_notification_badges.TestStaticContracts.test_kwin_window_attention_is_scoped_out. Verification: python3 -m unittest tests.test_dock_notification_badges -> 18 tests OK (pure node-vm helper tests incl. QVariant-sequence toArray, progress normalization, matching, upsert/replaces_id, transient/unmatched exclusion, stack aggregation, expiry; static wiring contracts; qmllint zero warnings; isolated headless E2E with private XDG dirs + private D-Bus session driving the REAL server over gdbus: critical+progress badge, client withdrawal, live progress replacement 30%->90%, client-supplied 2s expiry via sweeper, dismiss-on-attention, transient never badging and being expired at toast-hide, server bus-name ownership, plus the disabled-server no-badge degradation). Full suite: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -> 290 tests, OK, 2 pre-existing skips (bridge plugin not built); live Spotify/MPRIS environmental test passed in this run. Not verified on live hardware (offscreen E2E only): visual appearance of the ring/dot/badge composition, magnification interaction and real multi-monitor stacking remain manual test debt (live_verified false).

items.title: Monitör başına bağımsız Dock profilleri
items.evidence_note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-31 on feat/rush-orchestrator (commit bbe1ce5): per-monitor dock profile overrides keyed by output name. Pure resolution/sanitization in services/config/MonitorProfiles.js (.pragma library, node-testable); ConfigService gains dockMonitorProfiles (load-sanitized, persisted, mutation API setDockMonitorProfileKey / clearDockMonitorProfileKey / clearDockMonitorProfile, effectiveDockProfile(screenName), anyDockIntellihide window-tracking gate); Dock.qml resolves the effective profile per Variants delegate so monitor add/remove picks up/drops overrides without restart (screens model re-evaluates); DockItem popups and icon size follow the owning surface; SettingsWindow gains a Per-Monitor Dock Profiles editor card over the live screen model. Overridable keys: edge, floating, edgeOffset, iconSize, autoHide, intellihide. Pinned apps, stacks, monitor selection, magnification and delays stay global by design: Meta+1..9 shortcuts and stack markers address one merged dock row, so per-monitor pinned lists were scoped OUT (limitation, recorded). Backwards compatible: first-launch defaults untouched; configs without monitorProfiles load identically. Tests: python3 -m unittest tests.test_dock_monitor_profiles -> 24 tests OK (pure node-vm helper tests incl. simulated hotplug screen lists, static wiring contracts, qmllint zero warnings, isolated headless quickshell E2E: seeded load sanitization -> mutation API -> reactive binding update -> disk persistence -> fresh-process reload, plus fresh-defaults backwards compatibility). Full suite: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -> 272 tests OK, 2 pre-existing skips (bridge plugin not built); the known live Spotify/MPRIS environmental test passed in the recorded run. Known limitations / live-hardware debt: fractional-scale rendering and real monitor hotplug (Wayland output add/remove) not verifiable offscreen (offscreen platform exposes one unnamed screen, which correctly resolves to pure globals); manual verification on real hardware pending (live_verified false).
